preamble: Four solutions share the same definition and four other clues share another definition, neither forming part of the clues involved.

clue.text: What Scots eat is of poor quality, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word for shabby is spoken, and the answer sounds the same

parts.note: tatty means shabby or of poor quality

explanation.surface: A grumble about the dismal standard of Scottish cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: TATTY (shabby) and the Scots word for a potato are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots call a potato a tattie, a staple of their table such as in neeps and tatties.

clue.text: TV 6 (with women) getting demand for payment

definitions.meaning: a long-running police drama on British TV, its force including women officers as well as the men of 6 down

explanation.surface: Policemen on television presenting an invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Bill' is British slang for the police and the name of a long-running ITV police drama; 6 down is POLICEMEN, which with women officers makes the whole force.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is an invoice requiring payment; the police are known as the Old Bill.

clue.text: Ye began with this source of annoyance

definitions.meaning: the old runic letter for th, misread as y in the archaic spelling of the
a ... in one's side is a persistent irritant

explanation.surface: An archaic pronoun with a prickly beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ye' as in 'Ye Olde Shoppe' was originally written with the runic letter thorn (þ), standing for TH.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn is a prickle, and figuratively a persistent irritation.

clue.text: Yeltsin getting drunk with no expense spared

indicators.note: getting drunk means the name's letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: Boris Yeltsin drinking lavishly at a costly party.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Yeltsin, Russia's first president, was famous for heavy drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in style means doing it lavishly and elegantly.

clue.text: Fruit in two hands

indicators.note: two asks for the word for hands to be written twice in a row

parts.note: a paw is an informal word for a hand

explanation.surface: Someone holding a piece of fruit in both hands.
explanation.definitionFit: The papaya or the North American custard-apple fruit goes by this name.

clue.text: It's continued with, after apologies have been given

definitions.text: It's continued with, after apologies have been given

parts.words: It's continued with, after apologies have been given
parts.note: at a formal meeting apologies for absence come first and then the list of business is worked through

explanation.surface: Someone resuming after saying sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apologies' suggests contrition, but in meetings it is the first item, recording absences.
explanation.definitionFit: The list of business at a meeting is worked through once absences are noted.

clue.text: Officers in prison keeping order with insects invading

indicators.note: keeping means the jail word holds the rest inside it

parts.note: pen is short for penitentiary, a prison

indicators.note: invading says the insects get inside the order

parts.note: OM, the Order of Merit
lice are insects

explanation.surface: Prison officers keeping order during an infestation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Officers' looks like it belongs with 'prison', but it alone is the definition; OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Policemen are police officers.

clue.text: Opportunity around end of summer for hay being left to dry?

indicators.note: around means the opportunity word wraps the final letter

parts.note: a window is a window of opportunity

indicators.note: end of picks out the last letter of the season

explanation.surface: A chance at the end of summer for haymaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A windrow is a line of mown hay or crops left to dry in the wind.

clue.text: It's rotten chap that's out to bend the rules

indicators.note: out signals the words are put out of order

explanation.surface: A rotten fellow who is out to cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotten' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'out' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To stretch a point is to allow an exception or bend a rule.

clue.text: Cross about leading member of the Establishment

indicators.note: about means the hybrid animal goes around the royal letters

parts.note: a zo (or dzo) is a cross between a yak and a cow
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the monarch who heads the Establishment

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed about a figurehead of the ruling class.
explanation.walkthrough: This is one of the four answers sharing the undefined meaning 'duck': a duck in cricket is a score of nothing. 'Cross' looks like an adjective (angry) but is the Himalayan hybrid ZO.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a duck is a score of nought, so the shared definition fits.

clue.text: Filthy talk male abandoned coming to the female domain

indicators.note: abandoned says the letter for male is dropped from the dirty talk

parts.note: smut is obscene talk
her refers to a female
land is a domain or territory

explanation.surface: A man quits a woman's realm, leaving his crude talk behind.
explanation.walkthrough: One of four answers sharing the undefined meaning 'Donald': Donald Sutherland was a Canadian actor. SMUT loses M to give SUT; 'coming to' joins it to HER and LAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Sutherland was a celebrated film actor, so he answers to the first name Donald.

clue.text: Creator of Pluto — with money being spun!

definitions.text: Creator of Pluto — with money being spun!

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, also called Pluto

indicators.note: being spun means the currency word is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: the yen is Japanese money

explanation.surface: Walt Disney's cartoon dog made him a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: Pluto does double duty: Mickey Mouse's cartoon dog in the definition, and the Roman god of the underworld in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Walt Disney's studio created the cartoon dog Pluto and earned vast sums from it.

clue.text: Finish with nothing and grumble — you may have got the pip

definitions.text: you may have got the pip

parts.note: end means finish
O looks like zero, nothing
to carp is to grumble or complain

explanation.surface: Someone moaning their way to having the hump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got the pip' suggests being fed up, but it means literally containing the fruit stone.
explanation.definitionFit: The endocarp is the hard inner layer of a fruit that encloses the seed, as in a cherry stone.

clue.text: Delight to be had for nothing in days gone by

indicators.note: to be had for says the delight word is taken in exchange for the zero

parts.note: once means formerly, in days gone by
O looks like zero, nothing
to please is to delight

explanation.surface: Pleasure that once came free.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the four undefined 'Donald' answers: Donald Pleasence was an English actor. PLEASE replaces the O at the front of ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Pleasence was an English stage and screen actor, so he shares the first name Donald.

clue.text: A couple of brief illnesses bringing a complete change of mind

parts.note: a bout is a short spell of illness
a turn is a brief attack of illness, as in a funny turn

explanation.surface: Two short bouts of sickness make someone reverse a decision.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversal of opinion or policy, from the military drill command to face the other way.

clue.text: The first person to settle in the West Country

indicators.note: to settle in means the pronoun lodges inside the regional abbreviation

parts.note: SW, south-west, the West Country of England
me is the first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: A pioneer settler arriving in south-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: One of four undefined 'duck' answers. The West Country is south-west England (Devon, Cornwall, Somerset), abbreviated SW.
explanation.definitionFit: The smew is a small diving duck, a sawbill of northern waters.

clue.text: Wildly providing brief message that there's nothing to worry about?

indicators.note: brief means the message is shortened by dropping its opening pronoun

parts.words: message that there's nothing to worry about
parts.note: I am OK is a reassuring message

explanation.surface: Someone frantically sending word that all is well.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the I from I AM OK.
explanation.definitionFit: To run amok is to behave wildly and out of control.

clue.text: Hot men embraced by a timid sort, inadequately

indicators.note: embraced by means the soldiers are held inside
inadequately says the timid creature falls short by its last letter

parts.note: a mouse is a timid person
OR, other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Passionate men held by a shy person who can't cope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' reads as an adjective for the men, but it is the definition in its sense of passionate; OR (other ranks) is the usual crossword word for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot can mean sexually ardent, which is what amorous means.

clue.text: Rate bacon "bad" on account of salt

indicators.note: bad here means the letters of the phrase have gone off and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bacon judged bad because it is too salty.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbonate is a salt of carbonic acid, such as chalk.

clue.text: Front feverish — foes finally within striking distance at Agincourt

indicators.note: within places the last letter inside the other pieces

parts.note: the bow is the front of a ship
hot means feverish

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of the enemies word

explanation.surface: A hot front line, the enemy within range at the famous battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Agincourt (1415) was won by English longbowmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowshot is the distance an arrow can be shot, a measure of range for archers.

clue.text: Leaving party, dotty Irish drunk — not one needing a Guinness?

indicators.note: drunk tells us the remaining letters reel into a new order
Leaving says the party word departs from the crazy one

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: not means the numeral one is removed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A tipsy Irishman leaving a party, wanting another stout.
explanation.walkthrough: DOTTY minus DO is TTY; IRISH minus I is IRSH; these seven letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wants a drink of stout is parched.

clue.text: Quiet organ before start of evensong

parts.note: p, piano, is quiet in music
a lung is a body organ

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of the evening service

explanation.surface: A soft organ voluntary before evening worship.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the four undefined 'duck' answers: to duck is to dip or plunge. 'Organ' suggests church music, but it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck someone is to dunk them under water, as is to plunge them.

clue.text: Sole clot messing about? He had a funny partner

indicators.note: messing about means the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A lone idiot fooling around.
explanation.definitionFit: Lou Costello was the comic half of the double act Abbott and Costello.

clue.text: Don't just nibble your food!

parts.note: to wolf is to gulp food greedily rather than nibble
it stands for the food on your plate

explanation.surface: A command to eat heartily.
explanation.walkthrough: One of four undefined 'Donald' answers: Sir Donald Wolfit was an English actor-manager.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Donald Wolfit was a renowned English Shakespearean actor-manager, so he shares the name Donald.

clue.text: Revolutionary leader gets churned up inside

indicators.note: churned up inside says the three inner letters of the name are stirred into a new order

parts.note: Lenin led the Russian revolution

explanation.surface: A revolutionary leader with a churning stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: One of four undefined 'duck' answers: duck is a heavy cotton or linen cloth. The inner letters ENI of LENIN are rearranged as INE.
explanation.definitionFit: Duck is a strong close-woven fabric, traditionally of linen or cotton.

clue.text: A bit in the paper, one of about 2,000 Nelson was given?

definitions.meaning: a unit of newspaper space one column wide and an inch deep

definitions.text: one of about 2,000 Nelson was given?
definitions.meaning: Nelson's Column in London is about 2,000 inches tall, so each of those is an inch of a column

explanation.surface: A newspaper item about Nelson's honours.
explanation.walkthrough: Nelson's Column in Trafalgar Square is roughly 169 feet, about 2,000 inches, high.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspaper space is measured in units of one column by one inch.

clue.text: Huge agency makes a hospital suffer a setback

indicators.note: suffer a setback means the pieces go into reverse

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital

explanation.surface: A giant organisation reducing a hospital to crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: The US space agency is a vast government body.

clue.text: Evil place of illegal activity

parts.note: sin is evil-doing
a den, as in a den of thieves

explanation.surface: A wicked haunt of wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: One of four undefined 'Donald' answers: Sir Donald Sinden was an English actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Donald Sinden was an English stage and television actor, so he shares the name Donald.

clue.text: Malodorous fluid in filthy place

indicators.note: in places the liquid inside the dirty place

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty, any filthy place
ink is a writing fluid

explanation.surface: A smelly liquid in a dirty spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stinky gives off a bad smell.
